title.rendered: I Know the Plans I Have for You — Morning Devotional

excerpt.rendered: Jeremiah 29:11 was written to people in exile — not in their best season. Today’s devotional unpacks why that context changes everything about how we read God’s promise of a future and a hope.

content.rendered:
📖 Scripture

“For I know the plans I have for you, declares the Lord, plans for welfare and not for evil, to give you a future and a hope.”
— Jeremiah 29:11 (ESV)

📝 Message

Most people know Jeremiah 29:11. Fewer know who it was written to — and understanding the audience changes everything.

God spoke these words to a people in exile. Not a people in their best season, surrounded by blessing and ease. A people who had been taken from their homes by force, transported to a foreign land, and told to settle in for seventy years. Seventy years. That is not a short delay. That is a generation. That is your children growing up in a place that was never supposed to be your home.

And yet into that specific context — displacement, grief, waiting, confusion — God said: I know the plans I have for you.

Notice what He did not say. He did not say the plans are obvious. He did not say you will understand them soon. He did not say the exile will end quickly. He said: I know them. Even when you cannot see them. Even when the circumstances look like the opposite of a plan. Even when seventy years feels impossibly long.

The plans are not lost. They have not been revised because of what happened to you. They have not been cancelled because of your detours or your failures. God’s plans for you are plans for welfare, for a future, for hope — and they are held securely in His hands, not yours.

You do not need to know the plan today. You need to know the Planner. Trust Him with the details you cannot see. He has not lost the thread of your story.

🙏 Prayer

Father, thank You that You hold my future even when I cannot see it. I confess that uncertainty makes me anxious, and I sometimes mistake the silence for the absence of a plan. Remind me today that You are the God who spoke hope to exiles — and You speak the same hope over my life. I trust You with what I cannot see. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

🗣️ Declaration

God has plans for my life — plans for welfare, not for evil, plans for a future and a hope. My circumstances do not define my destiny. My delays are not denials. The God who holds the universe holds my story, and His plans for me are good. I will trust Him today with what I cannot yet see.

📖 Further Reading

  • Jeremiah 29:1–14 — Read the full context of this famous verse
  • Psalm 37:23–24 — The steps of a good man are ordered by the Lord
  • Proverbs 16:9 — In their hearts humans plan their course, but the Lord establishes their steps
  • Romans 8:28 — All things work together for good
  • Isaiah 46:10 — I make known the end from the beginning
  • Ephesians 2:10 — We are God’s handiwork, created for good works prepared in advance
